dedupe_keys.name: port of los angeles sea level rise adaptation study 2018

description: The Port of Los Angeles Sea Level Rise Adaptation Study, published by the port in 2018 and listed in California's ResilientCA Adaptation Clearinghouse, assesses how sea level rise will affect the port's state public trust lands. Coverage: the Port of Los Angeles on San Pedro Bay, one of the largest container ports in the United States. Content: it identifies the areas of public trust land projected to be exposed to sea level rise by 2030, 2050 and 2100, gives an overview of the vulnerabilities of the exposed facilities and presents a set of adaptation strategies that let the port adapt over time and stay resilient. The Clearinghouse tags it as a plan or strategy for the vulnerability assessment and adaptation framework phases of California's Adaptation Planning Guide. Format and access: the study is linked from the ResilientCA entry. Licence and cost: free to read; no licence stated. Caveats: the record rests on the Clearinghouse summary; exposure maps, scenarios and cost figures in the full study were not read here, and later port plans may update it. The exposure horizons and strategy set can frame hazard exposure and climate adaptation studies of container terminals and landside links. It relates to the Port of Los Angeles emergency station locations and the Port of London Authority adaptation update in the catalogue.
